title: ‘Kotu Kapima’ gambling ring expands as bets soar beyond Rs.100,000
byline: An illegal betting operation known locally as “Kotu Kapima” has emerged as a growing social and financial concern in Sri Lanka, with authorities warning that the underground scheme was attracting increasing numbers of gamblers and large sums of money.

title: Air India to test all pilots for banned substances
byline: Air India is to test all of its pilots for banned substances, starting immediately.

title: Police told to stop playing hide and seek when checking for traffic offences
byline: When a vehicle needs to be stopped for a traffic offence, police officers must carry out the interception openly and professionally at a location visible to other road users and should not hide in isolated locations or behind bushes while attempting to stop motorists, DIG in charge of the Traffic and Road Safety Range, W.P.J. Senadheera said.

title: Wattala shooting suspects deported from India
byline: Two suspects allegedly involved in a fatal shooting at a birthday party held at a hotel in Wattala on the night of July 23 have been arrested at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake after fleeing to India.

title: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms
byline: Thousands of US military members who have lived aboard an aircraft carrier for more than 250 days are reportedly contending with food shortages, broken plumbing and exhaustion, leading lawmakers to demand answers from the Pentagon and pressuring the Trump administration over the Iran war.

title: Mother and paramour arrested over abandonment of 4-year-old girl
byline: Police have arrested a woman and a man in connection with the abandonment of a four-year-old girl on Gammedda Road in Yatirawana Mudune, Wattegama yesterday.

title: Sri Lanka to lose GSP + if death sentence implemented
byline: The Government’s proposal for the re-introduction of capital punishment will have a direct bearing on its lobby to retaining the GSP+ trade facility when exporting to countries in the European Union (EU), which has traditionally opposed it.

title: 25,000 patients await surgery as heart list extends to 2029
byline: More than 25,000 patients across Sri Lanka are currently awaiting heart surgeries, major surgical procedures and essential medical tests, with the waiting list for some heart operations reportedly extending as far as 2029, raising fresh questions over the Government’s response to the country’s growing healthcare backlog.

title: Woman in Colombo arrested over Rs. 57M drug-linked assets
byline: A 53-year-old woman has been arrested by the Illegal Assets Investigation Division over properties and assets allegedly acquired through drug trafficking.

title: Japan confirms construction work of BIA 2nd terminal to begin before November
byline: Japan has confirmed that the construction work of the second passenger terminal at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) will commence before November this year.

title: Over 200,000 disputes referred to Mediation Boards annually
byline: More than 200,000 disputes are referred to mediation boards across Sri Lanka each year, the Ministry of Justice and National Integration said.

title: Unexpected guest: Croc on the loose at popular hotel
byline: A crocodile was found inside a banquet hall of a popular hotel in Battaramulla.

title: Viral video raises questions over police conduct
byline: A video circulating on social media has raised questions over police conduct during a routine vehicle check near the Wariyapola Police Station.

title: 22nd Amendment Bill to be tabled in Parliament on August 18
byline: Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara said the 22nd Constitutional Amendment Bill, which seeks to extend the retirement age of judges in Sri Lanka, will be presented to Parliament on Tuesday, August 18.

title: SJB accuses Justice Minister of putting showpiece on social media
byline: A video of Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara driving his vehicle came under fire by Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) MP Harshana Rajakaruna today.

title: Lal Kantha says he will not contest next parliamentary election from Kandy
byline: Agriculture Minister K.D. Lal Kantha has said he does not intend to contest the next parliamentary election from the Kandy District, while asserting that the National People’s Power (NPP) government will continue to remain in power.

title: Nearly 8,000 Police, tri-forces deployed for Kandy Esala Perahera security
byline: A comprehensive security and traffic plan has been implemented for the 2026 Kandy Esala Perahera, with more than 7,900 security personnel to be deployed throughout the festival period from August 18 to August 28.

title: President calls for stronger Co-operative network to regulate prices
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has stressed the need to strengthen Sri Lanka’s co-operative movement and state-owned retail institutions to play a more active role in the market and help regulate prices.

title: 50% Customs surcharge on vehicle imports extended until December
byline: The Government has extended until December 31, 2026, a 50% surcharge imposed on the applicable Customs Import Duty on specified imported motor vehicles.

title: Heat index likely to reach ‘Caution’ level in seven districts
byline: The heat index, or the temperature felt by the human body, is expected to rise to the ‘Caution’ level in several areas of seven districts during the daytime, the Department of Meteorology warned.

title: Notorious drug kingpin Shiran Basik brought back to Sri Lanka from Dubai
byline: Notorious drug trafficker Shiran Basik, who was arrested in Dubai, was brought back to Sri Lanka tonight (14), along with two other suspected underworld figures, under the custody of Sri Lankan law enforcement authorities.

title: Police to take legal action against vehicles obstructing bus stops
byline: The Sri Lanka Police has instructed all police stations to take legal action against drivers who park or leave vehicles in a manner that obstructs designated bus stops.

title: Residents demand probe into newly opened Chabad house in Hiriketiya
byline: Villagers and Buddhist monks in Hiriketiya have staged a protest calling for the removal of a recently established Chabad House in the popular southern coastal area.
